requirement:
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
rationale:
I found no gap, and no {fixme} is involved.

**Obligations and the code that carries them out**
- **Command form.** `Command::Author` in `src/main.rs` defines `--config`, `--missing` (conflicts with `--force` and `--stdout`), `--force`, `--stdout`, and `-v`/`--verbose`. It also defines the `author-evidence` alias.
- **Authoring one existing requirement or named example.** `AuthoringSubject::parse` turns the name into `Definition`. `author_evidence_with_options` calls `configured_assessment`, then `configured_record`, then `subject.sources` (`AssessmentSources::prepare`). `prepare` rejects any name that is not an existing non-Term definition ("no matching requirement or named example").
- **Under `--missing`, current evidence is kept without resolving configuration.** `author_evidence_with_options` returns `None` before configuration is resolved when `batch::subject_is_current` is true. It computes `force` as `options.force` or stdout output, so `--stdout` implies `--force`. `main` prints the "skipped as current" message in that case.
- **Completion report names the subject, backend, model and usage path.** `main` prints `"{subject}: {backend} / {model}; policy …"` followed by `Usage: <path>`. `configured_assessment` fills `AuthoringOutcome` with these values.
- **Evidence destination is the file path by default and "stdout" with `--stdout`.** In `main`, a present `evidence_path` prints `Evidence: <path>`. Otherwise it prints `Evidence: stdout`.
- **Stdout mode sends the report and diagnostics to stderr.**
  - `main` uses `eprintln!` for the report in stdout mode.
  - The false-judgment line and the verbose rationale also use `eprintln!`.
  - Coverage-loss failures use `eprintln!`, and errors propagate through `main`'s `Result`.
  - The `println!` of coverage-loss review reports cannot fire in stdout mode, because `replaced` is only populated for file output and so `review_losses` finds nothing to review.
- **Alias.** `#[command(alias = "author-evidence")]`.

**Tests**
- **`ollama_cli_delivers_sources…`** (`tests/authoring_cli.rs`). It runs `author-evidence` and checks the report prefix `SUBJECT: ollama / MODEL`, that `Evidence:` ends with `evidence/SUBJECT.json`, and that `Usage:` is present. This covers the alias and the default destination.
- **`stdout_emits_only_evidence_json…`**. It checks that stdout is only the JSON. It also checks that stderr contains the report, `Evidence: stdout` and `Usage:`, and that the false rationale appears only under verbose.
- **`verbose_single_author_reports…`**. It covers `-v` and `--verbose`.
- **`author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets`**. It covers an unknown subject.
- **`missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses…`** (`tests/authoring_batch.rs`). It covers:
  - `--missing` being the default and succeeding with a broken configuration, with no model call;
  - the `author-evidence` alias on a current record;
  - `--missing` and `--force` being mutually exclusive;
  - `--stdout` with `--missing` being rejected;
  - `--force` and `--stdout` reassessing.
- **`--config`**. It is exercised successfully in `false_is_a_completed_assessment` (`author-evidence … --config mock`) and in the batch test.

All obligations have reachable implementation and tests, and the extra behaviors in the implementing code (policy, coverage-loss reports, usage logging) are specified by other requirements the same code marks.

text: :::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} refresh
Every `habeas author` form MUST accept `--missing` and `--force`, which are
mutually exclusive; `--missing` MUST be the default. Under `--missing`, the
command MUST assess only the selected subjects whose evidence is missing, stale,
or invalid, and MUST preserve every current record without invoking a model,
including accepted FIXME judgments and current false judgments; a current false
judgment is reassessed only when its subject or inputs change or `--force` is
given. Under `--force`, the command MUST assess every selected subject. `--stdout`
MUST imply `--force`, because it writes no evidence. The command MUST report the
number of selected subjects it skipped as current. When no assessment is needed,
the command MUST succeed without resolving model configuration or credentials.
